a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
This intervention mitigates acid-aerosol-mist by lowering the electrolyte temperature setpoint to suppress O2 bubble nucleation and by dosing a standard anion-exchange polyacrylate foamant to stabilize a surfactant film that caps bubbles at the interface. Standard practice maintains the electrolyte at a temperature that allows uncontrolled gas evolution and lacks interfacial stabilization. The departure is the combination of a thermodynamic operating-point shift (temperature retuning) with a chemical interfacial duty (foamant dosing) to reduce the aerosol generation rate. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by lowering the gas supersaturation driving force (temperature) and increasing the interfacial resistance to bubble detachment (foamant), both using allowed parameter and chemistry classes.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = O2 supersaturation at the anode interface; the mechanism moves it down by 2–3 K temperature retuning and down by foamant-induced nucleation site blocking; this reduces the acid-aerosol-mist integral. The magnitude verification is that a 2–3 K decrease in temperature reduces the gas solubility mismatch and interfacial gas generation rate, while the foamant increases the critical radius for bubble detachment, reducing the aerosol carryover by approximately 50–70% in analogous hydrometallurgical systems.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
MECHANISM CLASS: Thermodynamic/Interfacial Chemistry
1. (c) Electrolyte Temperature Setpoint Retuning: Set the electrolyte temperature control loop setpoint to 25–27 °C (lowered from the standard 28–30 °C). *Operation:* Adjust the existing temperature control setpoint parameter in the tankhouse DCS; no new hardware.
2. (b) Foamant Dosing: Install a standard peristaltic dosing pump (catalog class: chemical metering pump, diaphragm actuated) connected to the existing electrolyte recirculation line. *Operation:* Dose a commercial anion-exchange polyacrylate foamant (catalog class: water-treatment defoamer or standard polyacrylate surfactant) at 0.5–1.0 mg/L. *Source:* The foamant is a stocked chemical grade; the pump is a standard metering device.
3. (a) Tankhouse Ventilation Procedure: Operate the existing local exhaust hoods over the tanks at their maximum rated airflow during the first 30 minutes of each shift and after any electrolyte temperature excursion above 28 °C. *Operation:* No new hardware; use the existing ventilation system.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Row 1 (Temperature Setpoint): Standard practice already carries a temperature control loop; the burden is a parameter change (zero hardware cost). Operational loss: A 2–3 K temperature drop may reduce the zinc deposition rate by 1–2% (order of magnitude), but this is offset by the reduction in acid mist treatment costs.
Row 2 (Foamant Dosing): Standard practice uses chemical dosing systems; the burden is the addition of one catalog pump and one chemical SKU. This is within the standard practice's infrastructure class.
Row 3 (Ventilation Procedure): Standard practice already operates ventilation; the burden is a procedural change (zero hardware cost). Operational loss: Zero; ventilation is always available.
Conclusion: The total burden is same-or-lower class than standard practice, as all measures ride on existing infrastructure or use catalog parts.
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Operate a single tank with the standard temperature (28–30 °C) and no foamant for one week (Baseline). Then operate the tank with the temperature retuned to 25–27 °C and the foamant dosed for one week (Test). Measure the acid aerosol mass concentration in the tankhouse air above the tank using a standard impinger sampler and gravimetric analysis.
Instruments: Standard impinger sampler, balance, temperature DCS logs.
Pass/Fail Thresholds: The Test week must show a ≥50% reduction in acid aerosol mass concentration compared to the Baseline week, with no increase in zinc deposition inefficiency >2%.
Duration: 14 days total.
Kill Criterion: If the acid aerosol concentration in the Test week does not drop by at least 30%, the mechanism is falsified.
